chunks: Musa ibn al-Qasim from Ibn Abi Umayr from Hammad from al-Halabi from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said:

Indeed, Uthman went out for Hajj, and when he reached al-Abwa', he ordered a crier to call out to the people: 'Make it a single Hajj and do not perform Tamattu'.' The crier called out, and as he passed by al-Miqdad ibn al-Aswad, he said: 'By Allah, you will find among the 'Qala'is' a man who will not accept what you say from him.' When the crier reached Ali (peace be upon him), who was at his beasts feeding them with bran and flour, upon hearing the call, he left them and went to Uthman and said: 'What is this that you have ordered?' He said: 'A opinion I have formed.' He said: 'By Allah, you have ordered contrary to the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family).' Then he turned away, facing away, raising his voice: 'Labbayk with Hajj and 'Umrah together, Labbayk.' And Marwan ibn al-Hakam used to say afterwards, as if I were looking at the whiteness of the flour mixed with the greenness of the bran on his arms.

key_terms.الْأَبْوَاءِ: Al-Abwa', a place near Mecca where the Prophet performed Hajj
key_terms.الْخَبَطُ: Bran or chaff, coarse food for animals or the poor
key_terms.الْقَلَائِصِ: A tribal group or specific people known for their stance
key_terms.تَمَتَّعُوا: Tamattu', a type of Hajj where one performs 'Umrah first, then Hajj
key_terms.لَبَّيْكَ: Labbayk, the declaration of readiness to perform the pilgrimage
key_terms.مَرْوَانُ بْنُ الْحَكَمِ: Marwan ibn al-Hakam, a prominent Umayyad figure

ai.seo_question: What was Ali's reaction to Uthman's change in Hajj ritual?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Isfahani highlights the jurisprudential dispute between Caliph Uthman and Imam Ali (AS) regarding the validity of Hajj al-Tamattu' versus Hajj al-Qira', with Ali asserting the Prophet's precedent. The vivid detail of Marwan observing the flour and bran on Ali's arms serves as a powerful symbol of Ali's active participation in the rituals alongside the common people, reinforcing his authority in distinguishing between political decree and prophetic tradition.
